files.content:
# Service renewals through the merchant operator

The operational renewal tools work on the same original case directory as the
merchant support console and renewal CLI. They carry an agreement from an expiry
queue through reviewed continuation terms, a source-bound quotation, the original
customer response, activation and a complete financial handover. The case writer
retains the terms and renewal histories together.

## Host configuration and access

Select the existing support provider and configure its support connection file's
`casesDirectory` and the private export root as described in
[SUPPORT.md](SUPPORT.md). The distribution contribution remains
`merchant-provider-support`; the renewal tools belong to that same provider.
They appear in the operator's catalog only when support is configured.

Use the host's existing authenticated HTTP or stdio MCP session and its current
tool grants. Proposal, decision and file release are mutation tools; the other
six operations are declared read-only. The operator keeps its original provider
dispatch, mutation concurrency checks, request-size limit and shutdown lifecycle.
The tools accept original record identities and values, rather than host paths or
credentials. The existing support owner closes its shared retained-file reader.

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `merchant_service_renewals_queue` | Page explicitly dated renewal work across the original case portfolio. |
| `merchant_service_renewals_read` | Open a case's terms, renewal history, eligible quotes and original customer responses. |
| `merchant_service_renewals_preview` | Review a continuation or quote attachment against current case and terms guards. |
| `merchant_service_renewals_propose` | Retain or revise that reviewed proposal, including its exact quotation attachment. |
| `merchant_service_renewals_decide` | Record acceptance, decline or closure through the original case writer. |
| `merchant_service_renewals_handover` | Return the complete validated handover object at a selected case revision. |
| `merchant_service_renewals_handover_file` | Receive that complete JSON in bounded, digest-pinned chunks. |
| `merchant_service_renewals_file_reads` | Inspect active handover reads for a case. |
| `merchant_service_renewals_file_release` | Release one unfinished read by its original read UUID. |

In the examples, `call(name, arguments)` means the existing MCP client's
`tools/call` operation with its original JSON result unwrapped. `caseId`,
`agreementId`, `actor`, `quoteId` and `continuationEndsAt` are the operator's
explicit selections. Generate new request and renewal identities with
`randomUUID()` from `node:crypto`.

## Inspect the full queue

```js
const selection = {
  asOf: new Date().toISOString(),
  noticeDays: 30,
  limit: 100
};
let offset = 0;
do {
  const page = await call('merchant_service_renewals_queue', {...selection, offset});
  await receiveRenewalRows(page.rows);
  offset = page.nextOffset;
} while (offset !== null);
```

Keep the same `asOf`, `through`, search and notice settings while paging.
The default horizon is 90 days after `asOf`; `through` can select another
exact UTC horizon. Times use the complete form `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ`.
Page size is 1–200, default 50. `q` searches case, agreement, merchant,
customer, owner, status and urgency fields.

The owner pages both the normal case index and archived cases before building
the queue. Expiring finite agreements appear as `unplanned` before a renewal
exists. Rows distinguish `expired`, `notice_due`, `upcoming` and
`resolved`; `caseStatus` preserves the original case metadata. A renewal's
retained notice date takes precedence over the default notice interval.
`includeClosed: true` includes closed renewals.

The returned summary describes the full dated portfolio before search and page
slicing. `total` describes the matching search result and `nextOffset`
continues that result. Inspect `unavailable` alongside the rows: it identifies
original case entries that could not be opened, with native failure details.

## Keep the four revision identities distinct

| Input or result | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Outer `id` | The original case UUID. |
| Outer `expectedRevision` | The current case SHA-256 revision required for a new change. |
| `input.id` | The selected renewal UUID, or a new UUID for a new renewal. |
| `input.expectedRevision` | The renewal edition number; explicit `null` creates a new renewal. |
| `input.termsId` | The original agreement's service-terms UUID. |
| `input.expectedTermsRevision` and `expectedTermsSha256` | The exact current service-terms edition and its retained SHA. |
| Outer `requestId` | A new UUID for one intended write, kept unchanged for every retry of that write. |

The wrapper binds the outer case revision and request ID into the complete
retained core request. Optional copies in `input.expectedCaseRevision` and
`input.requestId` must match the outer values. Most clients should supply
those values only at the outer level.

A current read exposes `case.revision` and `case.currentRevision`.
A historical read accepts `revision` and keeps the selected revision distinct
from the actual current head. New mutations always require the current head.

## Retain a reviewed continuation

Open the original case and inspect the exact agreement and any existing renewal
before choosing a new renewal UUID.

```js
const view = await call('merchant_service_renewals_read', {id: caseId});
const terms = view.termHeads.find(row => row.id === agreementId);
if (!terms) throw new Error('Choose a retained agreement in this case.');

const input = {
  id: randomUUID(),
  expectedRevision: null,
  termsId: terms.id,
  expectedTermsRevision: terms.revision,
  expectedTermsSha256: terms.sha256,
  continuation: {effectiveUntil: continuationEndsAt},
  actor,
  noticeDays: 30
};
const preview = await call('merchant_service_renewals_preview', {
  id: caseId,
  expectedRevision: view.case.currentRevision,
  input
});
const proposalRequest = {
  id: caseId,
  expectedRevision: view.case.currentRevision,
  requestId: randomUUID(),
  input: {...input, expectedPreviewSha256: preview.previewSha256}
};
const proposed = await call('merchant_service_renewals_propose', proposalRequest);
```

Retain `proposalRequest` before sending it. A new continuation requires an
explicit `effectiveUntil`; `null` selects an open-ended continuation.
For a normal active or ended finite agreement, omitted `effectiveFrom`
defaults to its original end. A later start is retained as an explicit gap.
Overlapping agreement periods are rejected.

The continuation can change title, customer, owner, dates, the complete service
calendar and response/recovery targets. Its incident-source identity, merchant
identity and merchant binding come from the original agreement. Preview returns
the exact continuation input, source/current term references, notice settings,
gap and `previewSha256`. Review those values before retaining the proposal.

A proposed continuation remains a distinct service-terms edition. Its original
source agreement and eventual activated continuation remain separate retained
editions under the same agreement identity.

## Quote the retained proposed edition

Use the existing `merchant_case_commercial` workflow to prepare, preview and
publish the quotation. Its `draft.serviceSourceId` must be the retained
continuation's `id + ':' + revision`. Include the original recurring service
line with `commitmentId` equal to that agreement UUID and the reviewed
quantity and monthly unit price. The native commercial desk captures the
complete service source binding, including the proposed terms SHA and snapshot.

Reopen `merchant_service_renewals_read` after publishing the quotation.
Each quote's `eligibleRenewalIds` identifies the proposed renewals to which
it actually binds. Attaching the quotation uses the current proposed terms
guards and omits continuation changes:

```js
const fresh = await call('merchant_service_renewals_read', {id: caseId});
const renewal = fresh.renewals.find(row => row.id === proposed.renewal.id);
const quote = fresh.quotes.find(row =>
  row.id === quoteId && row.eligibleRenewalIds.includes(renewal.id));
if (!quote) throw new Error('Choose the quotation of this retained continuation.');

const attachment = {
  id: renewal.id,
  expectedRevision: renewal.revision,
  termsId: renewal.continuationTerms.id,
  expectedTermsRevision: renewal.continuationTerms.revision,
  expectedTermsSha256: renewal.continuationTerms.sha256,
  actor,
  quoteId: quote.id,
  quoteSha256: quote.sha256
};
const review = await call('merchant_service_renewals_preview', {
  id: caseId, expectedRevision: fresh.case.currentRevision, input: attachment
});
const attachRequest = {
  id: caseId,
  expectedRevision: fresh.case.currentRevision,
  requestId: randomUUID(),
  input: {...attachment, expectedPreviewSha256: review.previewSha256}
};
const attached = await call('merchant_service_renewals_propose', attachRequest);
```

The native quotation controls remain `merchant_case_commercial_preview`,
`merchant_case_commercial_publish` and `merchant_case_commercial_receive`.
Keep the actual quotation and response request bodies for their existing replay
mechanism. Quote acceptance is recorded against that immutable quote before the
renewal decision activates its service terms.

Changing the continuation after a quote was attached creates a new proposed
edition. That edition needs a matching new quotation and original customer
response. The preceding quote's binding cannot authorize the changed terms.

## Record the original customer's decision

The commercial desk records the actual response, including its source and
observed time. Reopen the renewal view afterward. Accepted response options
carry `latest`; the decision must use the latest retained response for the
attached quotation, selected by observed time, recorded time and original ID.

```js
const current = await call('merchant_service_renewals_read', {id: caseId});
const selected = current.renewals.find(row => row.id === attached.renewal.id);
const response = current.acceptances.find(row =>
  row.latest &&
  row.payload.quoteId === selected.quote.id &&
  row.payload.quoteSha256 === selected.quote.sha256);
if (!response) throw new Error('Select the latest original accepted response.');

const acceptRequest = {
  id: caseId,
  expectedRevision: current.case.currentRevision,
  requestId: randomUUID(),
  input: {
    id: selected.id,
    expectedRevision: selected.revision,
    state: 'accepted',
    actor,
    acceptanceId: response.id,
    observedAt: response.payload.observedAt,
    reference: response.payload.source
  }
};
const accepted = await call('merchant_service_renewals_decide', acceptRequest);
```

Activation preserves the exact customer-reviewed dates, calendar, targets,
merchant binding and commercial material. The active terms become the next
edition immediately after the proposed continuation. The source, proposed and
activated editions remain in the original history.

The same decision tool records `declined` or `closed`, using the current
case and renewal guards and an original decision time. Closing requires a
nonempty `note`. A renewal may close after acceptance; its retained
`acceptedHead` still identifies the exact accepted edition for financial
receiving.

If another writer amended the service proposal, reopen it before proceeding.
After the obsolete renewal is declined or closed, a new renewal can use that
current proposed amendment when the terminal renewal anchors the original
active or ended agreement. Select the current terms guards and explicitly
provide the continuation end. The replacement preserves amended owner, dates,
calendar and targets while retaining a fresh proposed edition. Quote and accept
that new edition through the original commercial desk.

## Recover an interrupted change

Retry the exact original `propose` or `decide` request, including its old
case revision, renewal edition, request UUID and complete input. A retained
matching request reopens its original result before later case/terms guards and
returns `reused: true`. A changed body under that UUID is a conflict.

For a new operation, refresh the case and use its current guards. If an original
writer is busy, allow that operation to finish and retry the exact intended
request. The original store owns its writer lease and merge behavior; the
adapter adds no second writer queue.

| Native outcome | Recovery |
| --- | --- |
| `CASE_CONFLICT` | A fresh request selected a stale case. Open the case and review a new request. |
| `CASE_STORE_BUSY` or `OPERATOR_BUSY` | Finish the in-flight original operation, then retry the exact intended request. |
| `SERVICE_RENEWAL_OPERATION_CONFLICT` | The retained request identity was reused with different input. Recover the original body. |
| `SERVICE_RENEWAL_TERMS_CONFLICT` | The terms edition changed. Reopen current terms before reviewing another continuation. |
| `SERVICE_RENEWAL_QUOTE_CHANGED` | Select the quotation bound to the retained proposed edition. |
| `SERVICE_RENEWAL_RESPONSE_CHANGED` | A later customer response superseded the selected acceptance. |
| `SERVICE_RENEWAL_PREVIEW_CHANGED` | Preview the current complete proposal and retain that new review hash. |

The original error codes and statuses pass through the adapter. Support storage
errors retain the existing operator's path-sanitizing error handling.

## Receive the complete handover

For an ordinary result, call `merchant_service_renewals_handover` with
`{id: caseId, revision, renewalId}`. Pin the exact saved case revision when
receiving or forwarding a handover. The complete envelope contains:

- The selected immutable case summary and both complete original history arrays.
- The current selected renewal plus its exact `acceptedHead` reference.
- Distinct source terms, proposed continuation, activated terms and current terms
  within that selected case revision.
- The original quotation and customer response documents, material identities,
  full base64 material bytes and each original byte count/SHA.
- Exact continuity timestamps and gap, the financial join references, and the
  canonical handover seal.

The sealed case summary omits the changing current case head. Reopening the
same selected historical revision therefore reproduces the same envelope and
file bytes after later case edits. The normal read view still reports the
actual current head.

For large handovers, use the complete file reader:

```js
const choice = {
  id: caseId,
  revision: accepted.case.revision,
  renewalId: accepted.renewal.id
};
let part = await call('merchant_service_renewals_handover_file', {
  ...choice, limit: 65536
});
const descriptor = part.file;
const chunks = [Buffer.from(part.data, 'base64')];
while (part.nextOffset !== null) {
  part = await call('merchant_service_renewals_handover_file', {
    ...choice,
    readId: part.readId,
    expectedSha256: descriptor.sha256,
    offset: part.nextOffset,
    limit: 65536
  });
  chunks.push(Buffer.from(part.data, 'base64'));
}
const bytes = Buffer.concat(chunks);
if (bytes.length !== descriptor.bytes ||
    createHash('sha256').update(bytes).digest('hex') !== descriptor.sha256)
  throw new Error('The complete handover file did not match its descriptor.');
const renewalJson = new TextDecoder('utf-8', {fatal: true}).decode(bytes);
```

`createHash` above comes from `node:crypto`. Chunk offsets are bytes, and
the maximum chunk is 196,608 bytes. The last chunk returns
`nextOffset: null` and closes its retained read automatically. File status
is available with `merchant_service_renewals_file_reads({id: caseId})`.
Release an unfinished read with its original case ID and returned `readId`.

Retain the selection, descriptor and last received byte offset alongside the
download. After a process restart, expiration or completed-read reply loss,
omit `readId` and reopen the same selection with the retained
`expectedSha256` and offset. The original reader rejects a mismatched
selection or digest. A file digest covers the complete UTF-8 JSON bytes; the
handover's internal `sha256` covers its canonical envelope and is a separate
identity.

## Join the original financial calendar

The financial service agreement create/amend workflow receives the complete
`renewalJson` string beside `quoteContent` and `responseContent`.
Decode those two UTF-8 source strings from the handover's original
`materials.quote.data` and `materials.acceptance.data`; retain their
original byte counts and SHA values. They are the actual retained commercial
documents, including their envelopes.

The financial importer validates the full handover using the original
`validateServiceRenewalHandover(value)` export from the service renewal
module. It checks accepted-head identity, exact material bytes, source binding,
history and accepted interval before retaining its financial linkage.
`financialJoin.agreementId` is the original operational service-terms UUID;
the financial agreement keeps its own original calendar UUID.

For an existing financial agreement, amend its native terms at the original
calendar end with the accepted continuation and then extend the same calendar
through its original renew operation. Keep billing periods within the accepted
service interval. The operational renewal tools activate service terms and
produce this complete join; the original financial product performs the
calendar and billing changes.

# Retained merchant support through the original MCP operator

The merchant MCP can operate the same SF93 incidents, SF74 saved cases and SF77
workorders used by the merchant console. An agent can review saved registration
profiles, operate its own original watcher and notification recovery, read a recorded condition,
retain its original captures as a case, work through that case with the operator,
and produce a private support handoff and workorder. The original case directory
is shared with the support console; either interface can reopen the other's saved
versions.

These tools run through the existing authenticated HTTP or stdio provider.
Observation is explicit: `merchant_support_watch_start` runs the original SF93
watcher against its configured local merchant endpoints and delivers its configured
metadata-only notifications. The remaining source/case readers use retained data.
Acknowledgment and notification recovery use the same original transactions as
the terminal commands. Workorder preparation keeps customer acceptance and
external workorder delivery in the operator's existing commercial workflow.

## Operational service renewals

The same support provider exposes the complete saved agreement renewal workflow:
portfolio queue, reviewed continuation, original quotation and customer response,
service activation and a complete revision-pinned financial handover. Follow
[Service renewals through the merchant operator](SERVICE_RENEWALS.md) for the
nine tools, exact revision guards, replay and complete file receiving.

## Register the existing support inputs on the host

Create a private case directory, or use the existing directory passed to the
original `support-console --cases-dir` command. Keep its original privacy modes:
directories `0700`, source files `0600`. Prepare a support connection file:

```json
{
  "schema": "stellar-forge.merchant-support-connection.v1",
  "casesDirectory": "/private/merchant/cases",
  "incidentsDirectory": "/private/merchant/incidents",
  "profiles": {
    "current-host": {
      "label": "Current local merchant registration",
      "file": "/private/merchant/intake/watch.json"
    }
  },
  "handoffs": {
    "retained-case": {
      "label": "Current retained merchant support case",
      "file": "/private/merchant/intake/merchant-support.json"
    }
  },
  "workspaces": {
    "merchant-mapping": {
      "label": "Operator's saved merchant mapping and owner terms",
      "file": "/private/merchant/intake/merchant-workspace.json"
    }
  }
}
```

`casesDirectory` is required and must already exist. `incidentsDirectory` is
optional; when provided it is the original initialized SF93 state directory.
`handoffs` contains complete original SF74 support files. `workspaces` contains
original SF74 workspace files that provide a reviewed mapping for an incident's
route. `profiles` contains original SF93 watch configuration files for deliberate
registration or threshold changes. Each of these alias maps is optional and allows
up to 32 entries. Relative
paths resolve beside this support connection file. MCP inputs never select a
filesystem path.

Add `"supportConnection": "/private/merchant/support-connection.json"` to the
existing `merchant-mcp.json`, then restart the MCP host. For a new merchant, add
`--support /private/merchant/support-connection.json` to the existing `serve.mjs
init` command. Its OpenAPI, saved-package, Python and DuckDB initialization modes all
support this option. The original source aliases, release history, running seller
and catalog connection retain their usual meanings. A support connection can
also be used with an existing host configuration whose source alias map is empty;
case operation does not require an active seller release.

The customer export root from `exportsDirectory` must be a real private directory.
Support exports use named new subdirectories there, alongside the existing
customer SDK exports. The connection stores references to the original inputs;
it does not copy an incident store. Applying a profile explicitly changes the
original capture configuration through SF93's existing transaction.

## Operate the original observer and notification recovery

Initialize the incident directory once on its host with the existing SF93 command
and a private watch configuration. The original
[incident operations guide](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf93-seller-support-bundle/INCIDENT_OPERATIONS.md)
describes local seller/operations origins, thresholds, capture retention and the
metadata-only webhook contract. For example, from the source checkout:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf93-seller-support-bundle/incident-cli.mjs init \
  --state /private/merchant/incidents --config /private/merchant/intake/watch.json
```

Supply the notification URL and signing key using the original configuration's
environment references when starting the MCP host. Neither value is an MCP
argument, profile value or returned notification field. Profiles name those
environment references and retain the original local merchant origins and
thresholds, so the operator can inspect what a change will observe. Editing a
profile file alone does not change the running watcher.

| Tool | Operation |
| --- | --- |
| `merchant_support_profiles` | List declared profiles and the current original configuration, or inspect one profile, its digest and concrete merchant/settings changes. |
| `merchant_support_configure` | Apply the inspected profile with its exact file digest and current integer configuration revision. |
| `merchant_support_watch_status` | Read the saved original worker record, this MCP process's owned instance and its last completion/failure. |
| `merchant_support_watch_start` | Acquire the original worker lease and start observation for the exact inspected configuration revision/hash. |
| `merchant_support_watch_stop` | Abort and await only this MCP process's watcher, using its exact returned instance ID. |
| `merchant_notifications` | Inspect/filter/page original events, their attempts, delivery state and retry reason. |
| `merchant_incident_notify` | Queue a new reminder for the exact incident revision using the currently configured destination. |
| `merchant_notification_update` | Retry an original paused/exhausted event, or cancel an unfinished event, with its exact attempt count and named operator. |

Start with `merchant_support_profiles` without arguments. Inspect a declared
profile when its original merchant registration, thresholds or notification
settings need changing:

```json
{"profile":"current-host"}
```

The result includes the compiled original `configuration`, `sourceSha256`,
`configHash`, `current.configRevision`, and changes to merchant registrations,
their order and other settings. Apply precisely that inspected source:

```json
{
  "profile":"current-host",
  "expectedSourceSha256":"<sourceSha256 from profile inspection>",
  "expectedConfigRevision":1
}
```

An unchanged profile retains its existing configuration revision. Use the
returned values instead of assuming the revision increased. Use that current
revision and configuration hash to call
`merchant_support_watch_start`:

```json
{"expectedConfigRevision":2,"expectedConfigHash":"<current original configHash>"}
```

The original startup transaction checks both expectations while it owns the
worker lease. A concurrently changed configuration is refused before replacing
the saved worker record or polling. Existing CLI/service launches remain
compatible. A worker already holding that directory's kernel lease remains its
owner; MCP reports the original lease conflict and cannot stop that worker.

Retain the returned `owned.instanceId`. `owned.startedConfiguration` records the
configuration accepted at this start; top-level `configRevision`/`configHash`
describe the current store, including a later explicit profile change. The
original worker notices configuration changes through its existing sweep logic.
Changes that retire a registration retain the original `RETIRED` distinction;
they do not become observed recovery.

After a lost start response, inspect `merchant_support_watch_status`. Its `owned`
field identifies this MCP process's actual watcher. The saved `worker` record is
also useful after a crash, but a saved `RUNNING` status alone does not establish
that a worker is still alive. A new process uses the original kernel lease when
it starts; it does not kill a saved PID or remove an ownership file. A startup or
background failure is retained in `lastOwnedExit` with its original safe code.

Read `merchant_incidents` and `merchant_notifications` to work the actual observed
condition. An event with `EXHAUSTED` or `PAUSED` may be retried using its current
attempt count, for example through `merchant_notification_update`:

```json
{"id":"<original event UUID>","expectedAttempts":3,"action":"retry","by":"Merchant operator"}
```

This continues the same original event/body/destination. The original engine
refuses an in-flight or completed event, a stale attempt count, or a changed
destination/configuration. After repairing the existing destination, retry that
event when its original rules allow it. If intentionally selecting a new
destination, inspect the current incident revision and call
`merchant_incident_notify`; this queues a **new** original reminder. Cancel an
unfinished previous event with the same `merchant_notification_update` tool and
`action:"cancel"` when the operator intends that cancellation. Cancellation does
not erase the incident or report its merchant condition as recovered. After an
interrupted notification mutation, inspect the original events before issuing
another reminder; reminders create new event identities.

Stop an owned watcher with `merchant_support_watch_stop` and its exact
`instanceId`. It waits for the current original state write and lease release;
repeating that same completed stop in the same MCP process returns `unchanged`.
Closing the MCP host performs the same owned-watch shutdown alongside its other
owned runtimes. It does not stop an independently run watcher, seller, notification
receiver or delivery worker. The incident store, captures, events and cases stay
available to the next MCP process and the original terminal/browser interfaces.

Once the native observer captures the active or recovered condition, continue
below with `merchant_incident_case`, using the exact incident revision, inspected
workspace template and original route ID. That creates the same versioned support
case used for owner terms, workorder and private handoff.

## Complete case and workorder workflow

| Tool | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `merchant_support_sources` | List configured aliases, or inspect a handoff/template with its exact source digest and mapping. |
| `merchant_incidents` | Read original condition, revision, captures, acknowledgment and notification state. Filter by ID or status and page through the result. |
| `merchant_incident_ack` | Acknowledge an original open incident using its exact integer revision and named operator. |
| `merchant_incident_case` | Use an inspected workspace template and the original incident export to create a saved case. |
| `merchant_cases` | Find cases by text, work status or follow-up date. Archived cases appear when selected explicitly. |
| `merchant_case_import` | Import an inspected, complete original support handoff into a new case UUID. |
| `merchant_case_read` | Reopen the current or a retained revision, including actual source identities, runtime review and raw unfinished owner terms. |
| `merchant_case_history` | Page through the original immutable case versions. |
| `merchant_case_update` | Save owner metadata, terms or source selection against an exact current revision. |
| `merchant_case_restore` | Restore an earlier version as a new current version, retaining the intervening history. |
| `merchant_case_workorder` | Generate the original workorder from an exact saved revision and its selected sources. |
| `merchant_case_export` | Publish the original workspace, support handoff and readable review; optionally include the workorder documents. |
| `merchant_support_export_status` | Verify a retained export's completion manifest and original file hashes. |
| `merchant_support_export_manifest` | Inspect the retained completion manifest, its own exact digest, and this operator's read sessions. |
| `merchant_support_export_file` | Retrieve an original file with its manifest digest, file digest and byte offset. |
| `merchant_support_export_file_release` | Release only this operator's temporary read snapshot. |

### Open the actual retained source

First call `merchant_support_sources` without arguments. Inspect the chosen input:

```json
{"kind":"handoff","source":"retained-case"}
```

The response gives its actual `sourceSha256`, saved merchant mapping, source
coverage and original runtime review. To retain it as a case, call
`merchant_case_import` with that alias, the exact returned digest and a newly
chosen UUID in `id`. Import keeps the original workspace text, support text,
metadata, unfinished terms and source choice. A changed host file is rejected;
inspect it again before importing the new version.

Alternatively, read `merchant_incidents`. Its incident `revision` is an integer,
which differs from the SHA-256 revision of an SF74 case. An acknowledgment takes
`id`, `expectedRevision`, `by` and optional `notes`. An acknowledged incident stays
under the original watcher's recovery logic. MCP cannot mark it recovered.

For `merchant_incident_case`, supply a new case UUID in `id`, the original
`incidentId` and `expectedIncidentRevision`, a configured workspace alias in
`template`, its inspected `expectedTemplateSha256`, and the actual `routeId` in
the retained capture. SF93 exports the original before/follow-up packets through
its existing operator function. The importer retains its exact case metadata,
including incident identity, timestamps and acknowledgment, in the original SF74
store. It snapshots the inspected template before passing it to SF93, so a host
edit cannot silently change that mapping during export. The temporary SF93 export
is removed after the original case save; retained capture bytes live in the saved
case and remain available through its complete handoff.

### Record the owner's work and reopen it

`merchant_case_read` returns the current revision, selected source mode, raw
`termsText`, parsed terms where possible, and the original runtime review. It
returns original source hashes and findings; large source payloads stay in the
private store. The runtime review retains actual day/session/path variants,
source coverage and complete network/asset/amount/recipient option groups. The
case itself does not change when it is read.

Update a case with `id`, its exact `expectedRevision`, and any of these fields:

- `metadata`: a partial change to merchant, owner, work status, follow-up date,
  next action or notes. Other metadata stays unchanged.
- `terms`: the original SF77 owner terms document, including its explicit
  merchant-consent and commercial-proposal states. Delivery scope, deliverables
  and acceptance criteria are optional multiline text fields.
- `workorderSource`: `runtime` for attached original runtime sources, or
  `diagnostic` for the existing SF70/SF76 diagnosis workflow.
- `baselineOnly`: the existing diagnostic baseline selection.

For example, after reading the actual case revision, record an unfinished
internal scope using the same terms format as the support console:

```json
{
  "workOrderRef": "YOUR_WORK_REFERENCE",
  "sellerDisplayName": "YOUR_MERCHANT",
  "relationshipOwner": "YOUR_RELATIONSHIP_OWNER",
  "proposedWindow": "UNSCHEDULED",
  "delivery": {
    "scope": "Owner-entered scope and exclusions",
    "deliverables": "Owner-entered deliverables",
    "acceptanceCriteria": "Owner-entered review criteria"
  },
  "merchantConsent": {"status":"NOT_RECORDED","receiptUrl":null},
  "commercial": {
    "priceApproval":"NOT_APPROVED",
    "feeUsd":null,
    "costUsd":null,
    "approvalReceiptUrl":null
  }
}
```

Pass this document as `terms` in `merchant_case_update`. Actual existing consent
or owner approval uses the original SF77 states and receipt fields; the original
workorder assembler validates that proposal. No fee or approval is inferred from
a source report, a blank cost field or the case's work status. Incomplete drafts
can be saved and corrected before preparing a workorder. Omitted terms preserve
the exact prior raw form values, including hidden or unfinished entries.

The browser and MCP share the original terms document↔draft converter. Open the
same case directory in `support-console`; the merchant mapping, delivery text,
source selection and original captures appear in the existing form. Saving in
either interface creates the next original version. An agent reading a version
before a browser change cannot overwrite that change with stale terms.

`merchant_case_history` returns `nextBefore` for another page. To restore a
version, pass its `revision` and the currently selected `expectedRevision` to
`merchant_case_restore`. This adds a version containing the earlier original
workspace, support and metadata. It does not delete later history.

### Prepare and export the actual workorder

Call `merchant_case_workorder` with `id` and `expectedRevision`. It uses the same
original source assembler as `/api/workorder` in the support console. Runtime
mode uses the attached captures and recorded mapping; diagnostic mode uses the
saved before/after sources and baseline selection. Both paths retain the original
SF77 commercial and acceptance semantics. The packet identifies the exact case
revision and the hashes of its original workspace and support.

`merchant_case_export` takes the same selection and a new `exportId`. With
`includeWorkorder:true`, it writes:

- `case.json` and `merchant-workspace.json` for the selected original version;
- `merchant-support.json` and `support.html` when the case has runtime sources;
- `owner-terms.json`, `packet.json`, `seller-packet.html` and
  `acceptance-checklist.md` when the workorder is requested;
- `support-export.json`, written last, identifying the completed export and each
  original file's byte count and SHA-256.

The complete support handoff reopens directly in the existing SF74 console.
The original SF77 CLI can also consume `merchant-support.json` with
`owner-terms.json`. This MCP join introduces no new handoff or contract format.
Use the existing private business delivery workflow to provide the completed
files to the intended recipient.

## Retrieve and reopen the private handoff

The same MCP service now returns the actual retained export bytes. The client
saves the original file names, case/workspace/support content, workorder documents
and completion manifest. It does not rerun an observer, seller, workorder or
export. Files from the original two-file diagnostic export, four-file runtime
export and their workorder additions use the same manifest format.

From the complete source checkout or a cumulative package containing this source,
start the existing merchant MCP listener with its usual host configuration and
bearer environment. On the receiving Linux machine, supply that endpoint's bearer
through `MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN` or an existing variable named with `--token-env`. Use the
original loopback listener, an operator-established SSH tunnel, or the host's
existing HTTPS endpoint. Tokens never appear in command arguments, progress,
download checkpoints or exported files. The client refuses redirects, URL
credentials and bearer transport over non-loopback HTTP.

```sh
starforge merchant-mcp download-support \
  --url http://127.0.0.1:3211 \
  --export-id recovered-incident \
  --out /private/received/recovered-incident
```

Before delivery, `starforge merchant-mcp inspect-support --url MCP_ENDPOINT
--export-id EXPORT_ID` returns `{manifest,manifestSha256}`. Pass the reviewed
digest to `download-support --manifest-sha256 REVIEWED_DIGEST` to require that
exact receipt before the client creates or changes local output. The embedding
API is `inspectSupportExport({url,exportId,tokenEnv,environment,signal})`;
`downloadSupportExport` accepts the optional `expectedManifestSha256`.

The source equivalent begins with
`node stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/serve.mjs download-support` and takes
the same options. The output's parent directory must already exist. The command
creates its private output directory with mode `0700` and files with mode `0600`.
An existing output is accepted only as this same download; unrelated files and a
different endpoint/export/manifest are rejected without replacing them. Its
`download-state` directory retains the original manifest, per-file byte/hash
checkpoints and a Linux kernel lease. Install `flock` from util-linux on the
receiver, as used by the original merchant state stores. The lease prevents two
clients from writing the same output and is released automatically on process
exit, including an unexpected termination.

Each chunk is checked against the original export ID, manifest SHA-256, filename,
complete file SHA-256, byte count and offset. The default chunk is 196,608 bytes;
`--chunk-bytes` can select a smaller positive value for an existing constrained
transport. Progress is a JSON line on stderr. The final JSON on stdout reports
`COMPLETE`, the original case identity, exact manifest digest and completed file
counts. `support-export.json` appears at the output root only after all original
files have been checked and published there. Its publication is atomic, preserving
resume after a stopped completion write. The files remain directly usable by
the existing console and private business delivery workflow.

### Continue after a lost connection or process exit

Run the **same command with the same output directory**. Completed files are
rehash-checked locally and retained. A partial file resumes from its saved byte
offset after the durable prefix is verified. An uncheckpointed suffix left by a
killed write is discarded within that owned partial file; the verified prefix
is preserved. A changed completed or checkpointed file is reported instead of
being overwritten. Disk-full and connection errors leave the original partial
state available for the next invocation after the host issue is corrected.

Read IDs identify the server process's temporary snapshots. If the server restarted
or the read expired, the client opens the same original file at its saved offset
with both original digests. It cannot combine chunks from another manifest or
silently select a newer case revision. A graceful interruption releases its
current read; an abrupt client exit leaves that snapshot to the original idle
expiry. Closing the server releases its owned snapshots while retaining the
export. The client never shuts down the server or another operator's watcher.

### Reopen through the existing case desk

To save the downloaded source into a local original SF74 case directory, add
`--cases-dir /private/merchant/cases` to the download command. The private case
directory must already exist. For an already completed download, the same
continuation works offline:

```sh
starforge merchant-mcp reopen-support \
  --dir /private/received/recovered-incident \
  --cases-dir /private/merchant/cases

starforge support-console --cases-dir /private/merchant/cases
```

Reopening verifies the saved files, invokes the original SF74 handoff importer
and saves through its original case writer. Diagnostic-only exports reuse their
original workspace and case metadata. A new local case UUID is recorded before
the save, so an interrupted reply resumes the same import. Subsequent invocations
reopen that local case and preserve later browser/MCP edits. If the initial save
completed before its download checkpoint and the local case was subsequently
edited, reopening traverses the original case history, verifies its first imported
revision and keeps the current edited head. The result identifies
both the original exported case and the local case/revision; it does not overwrite
an existing case using the remote UUID. One download retains one local case-directory
binding, while the original files remain portable through the normal console
import. Original case writer recovery remains in [CASE_DESK.md](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf74-merchant-support-console/CASE_DESK.md).

Open the returned case in the existing console to continue its source comparison,
follow-up, recorded fees, acceptance text and workorder. Reopening changes neither
the retained observation times nor the commercial approval state. No MCP server,
merchant endpoint, observer, payment adapter or notification receiver is contacted
by `reopen-support`.

### Use the retained-file tools from an existing MCP client

Call `merchant_support_export_manifest` with `exportId`. `MANIFEST_RETAINED`
means that the original completion manifest exists and parses; it does not reread
all payloads. The response's `manifestFile` gives the exact original manifest
name, bytes and SHA-256. The existing `merchant_support_export_status` remains
the explicit full-file verification operation and returns its unchanged
`COMPLETE`, `NOT_FOUND` or `INCOMPLETE_OR_OTHER_EXPORT` meanings.

Retrieve `support-export.json` or a filename present in that original manifest:

```json
{
  "exportId":"recovered-incident",
  "file":"merchant-support.json",
  "expectedManifestSha256":"<manifestFile.sha256>",
  "expectedSha256":"<that original file's sha256>",
  "offset":0,
  "limit":65536
}
```

The result contains `readId`, `file`, `offset`, `bytesRead`, `nextOffset`,
`encoding:"base64"` and `data`, plus the pinned export/manifest identity. Continue
with that same `readId`, both digests and `nextOffset`. `nextOffset:null` completes
and releases the snapshot. A resumed offset or read ID requires `expectedSha256`.
After `SUPPORT_READ_NOT_FOUND`, omit the old read ID and retain the original
digests/offset. `merchant_support_export_file_release` takes the `exportId` and
`readId` when the client deliberately abandons a read.

Support, accounting and customer SDK exports share the original accounting reader
implementation; each
native owner retains its own lifecycle. Each owner permits four concurrent
verified snapshots totaling 256,000,000 bytes, retains up to 32 KiB in memory per
small file, and uses an immediately unlinked private descriptor for larger files.
Later chunks reuse the snapshot without rereading the entire source. Original
files stay in their existing export/workspace, and unfinished snapshots expire
after 120 seconds idle. Support's manifest view reports original loader counts
and active snapshot metadata without host paths. Accounting's tool names,
selectors, result fields, original-read counts and workspace-close behavior
remain unchanged.

## Concurrent edits, interruption and private state

All mutating support calls use the existing merchant operator's serialization.
The original SF74 writer lock and expected revision also protect against another
console process. Import and a repeated identical case update/restore use the
original store's retry semantics; read the actual saved case after an interrupted
reply. A stale request with different content is rejected. Incident acknowledgment
uses the original SF93 integer revision and transaction lease. A stale incident
or changed input file requires a fresh inspection.

Exports are exclusive: an existing ID is never replaced. If the reply is lost,
call `merchant_support_export_status` with that ID. `COMPLETE` means the final
manifest and all referenced original file bytes match. `NOT_FOUND` means that
named directory is absent. `INCOMPLETE_OR_OTHER_EXPORT` means the directory has
no completed support manifest; inspect it locally and choose a new ID for a new
export. Source/manifest disagreement is reported explicitly. The operator does
not silently republish over a partial export or a customer SDK delivery.

Private filesystem errors omit host paths in MCP tool responses. The host retains
its original incident/case files, existing locks and export permissions. The
original support CLI remains the explicit mechanism for stopped-process writer
recovery. Closing or restarting MCP changes no case source, incident observation
or completed customer export.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Original streaming source archive, with the SF49 envelope and limits."""
from __future__ import annotations
import importlib.util
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys

SCHEMA = "stellar-forge.sf49.source-edition-archive.v1"
MAX_META = 2 * 1024 * 1024
MAX_SOURCE = 16 * 1024 ** 3
MAX_FILE = 8 * 1024 ** 3


def module():
    original = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "scf-starforge-20261009" / "sf30-seller-sdk" / "source_bundle_archive.py"
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("sf49_source_bundle_archive", original)
    value = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(value)
    return value


def main():
    try:
        raw = sys.stdin.buffer.read(MAX_META + 1)
        if len(raw) > MAX_META:
            raise ValueError("Archive request exceeds the retained metadata limit")
        request = json.loads(raw)
        if not isinstance(request, dict) or request.get("action") not in ("archive", "extract", "inspect"):
            raise ValueError("Use a native source archive action")
        # The maintained Node carrier obtains this from SF74's exported
        # MAX_HANDOFF_BYTES, including the installed workspace/Service schema.
        # This private child field is never part of the public upload request.
        handoff_bytes = request.pop("nativeHandoffBytes", None)
        if type(handoff_bytes) is not int or not 0 < handoff_bytes <= MAX_FILE:
            raise ValueError("Use the original server-derived handoff allowance")
        max_expanded = MAX_SOURCE + handoff_bytes + 3 * MAX_META
        shared = module()
        policy = shared.ArchivePolicy(SCHEMA, max_expanded_bytes=max_expanded,
                                      max_members=72, max_manifest_bytes=MAX_META,
                                      max_file_bytes=MAX_FILE,
                                      receipt_name=None, prefix="SF49")
        result = getattr(shared, request["action"])(request, policy=policy)
        sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({"ok": True, "result": result}, ensure_ascii=False,
                                    separators=(",", ":"), allow_nan=False) + "\n")
        return 0
    except Exception as error:
        code = getattr(error, "code", "SF49_ARCHIVE_INPUT_OR_IO_FAILED")
        sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({"ok": False, "error": code,
                                    "errno": getattr(error, "errno", None),
                                    "message": getattr(error, "message", "The original source archive operation could not complete.")},
                                   ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n")
        return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

# Service renewals

Service renewals follow the original case, agreement terms, commercial quote, and customer response. The portfolio queue shows finite agreements approaching their notice or ending dates. Each retained proposal keeps the original agreement edition, its proposed continuation, the owner, the notice date, and the quotation of that exact continuation. An accepted renewal creates the next active terms edition using the latest accepted response to that quotation.

The case remains the storage and revision boundary. Renewals are retained in the optional `service.renewals` history inside the existing workspace. Support text, case metadata, and the other workspace sections continue through the original case writer.

## Operator workflow

1. Open the renewal queue at an explicit UTC time and choose an agreement. Read the selected case to obtain its current case revision and exact terms edition.
2. Prepare a continuation. Keep its original agreement ID and merchant/incident binding. The continuation begins at or after the source agreement ends. Enter its ending timestamp, or `null` for an open-ended continuation. A later beginning is recorded as a gap.
3. Preview and retain the proposal. This creates a proposed terms edition in the original agreement history. Assign a renewal UUID once and use a distinct request UUID for each intentional change.
4. Use the existing commercial desk to publish a quote of that exact proposed terms edition. Include a recurring-service line whose source points to the proposed edition and original agreement row. Return to the renewal, select that quote, and retain the attachment without changing its continuation.
5. Record the customer's response through the original commercial receiving workflow. Accept the renewal using the latest retained accepted response to its exact quote. The renewal decision's `observedAt` is the original response timestamp. The resulting active edition preserves the reviewed continuation's period and service commitments.
6. Export the handover for the financial workflow. It carries source, proposed, activated, and current terms; the original quote and response documents; exact material bytes; and their case, agreement, document, and hash joins.

Declining retains the proposal and its recorded decision. Closing records an explanatory note while preserving earlier decisions and acceptance. If the agreement is amended while a proposal is open, close or decline the old proposal, then reopen the case and its current terms before creating a replacement.

A replacement uses a fresh renewal UUID and the current proposed terms revision and hash. The latest retained active or ended agreement must be the exact original source anchored by the closed or declined renewal. The replacement carries forward the amended owner, dates, and service targets under the current case and terms guards, and retains a fresh proposed edition. Publish a quote of that new edition and record its own customer acceptance before activation.

## Case API

Create the desk with the original store and workspace identity:

~~~javascript
import {openCaseServiceRenewals} from './case-service-renewals.mjs';
import {commercialWorkspaceId} from './case-commercial.mjs';

const renewals = openCaseServiceRenewals({
  caseStore,
  workspaceId: commercialWorkspaceId(casesDirectory)
});
~~~

The factory also accepts the existing `commercialDesk` as an identity source when `workspaceId` is omitted.

| Method | Arguments | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `queue` | `{asOf, through?, noticeDays?, offset?, limit?, q?, includeClosed?}` | Portfolio rows, urgency summary, pagination, and unavailable cases |
| `read` | `{id, revision?}` | Case, terms and renewal history, current editions, quotes, responses, and accepted-response choices |
| `preview` | `{id, expectedRevision, input}` | Core proposal preview and case summary |
| `propose` | `{id, expectedRevision, requestId, input}` | Saved case view, exact renewal, changed terms, and retry status |
| `decide` | `{id, expectedRevision, requestId, input}` | Saved case view, exact renewal, changed terms, and retry status |
| `handover` | `{id, revision?, renewalId}` | Complete original-case handover JSON with a content hash |

Here `id` is the case UUID. Inside `input`, `id` is the renewal UUID and `expectedRevision` is its integer edition, or `null` for a new proposal. The outer `expectedRevision` is the case's SHA-256 revision.

`read.terms` and `read.renewalHistory` carry full history. `read.termHeads` and `read.renewals` carry the latest editions. Quote choices retain the original quote fields and add `eligibleRenewalIds` and `latestResponseId`. Accepted-response rows retain the original document and add `latest`; only a latest accepted response is eligible for activation.

The queue scans both the ordinary and archived sections of the original case index before sorting, filtering, and paginating agreement rows. Each row includes its original case status; unreadable case IDs are deduplicated across pages. Search covers case, agreement, customer, owner, merchant, state, and urgency. The returned `summary` describes the full readable portfolio; `total` is the number of rows matching the search. `unavailable` identifies cases that could not be opened. The default page has 50 rows and the maximum is 200. An omitted horizon ends 90 days after `asOf`.

## Command line

Use the same case directory as the console. Output is JSON; redirect it to a file when needed.

~~~sh
node service-renewals-cli.mjs ids
node service-renewals-cli.mjs queue \
  --cases-dir "$CASES_DIR" \
  --as-of 2026-10-12T12:00:00.000Z \
  --through 2027-01-10T12:00:00.000Z \
  --notice-days 30
node service-renewals-cli.mjs read \
  --cases-dir "$CASES_DIR" --case "$CASE_ID"
~~~

A new proposal's input file has the following structure. Replace the example IDs, hash, terms edition, dates, and reviewer with the selected case's original values.

~~~json
{
  "id": "1e836b1d-7f85-4550-9d67-7856c923c321",
  "expectedRevision": null,
  "termsId": "e37bf55b-126b-4dc7-bf03-0c45c1071932",
  "expectedTermsRevision": 1,
  "expectedTermsSha256": "<64-character original terms SHA-256>",
  "continuation": {
    "effectiveFrom": "2026-11-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "effectiveUntil": "2027-11-01T00:00:00.000Z"
  },
  "noticeDays": 30,
  "owner": "Service owner",
  "actor": "Reviewer",
  "note": "Continue the reviewed service commitments for one year."
}
~~~

~~~sh
node service-renewals-cli.mjs preview \
  --cases-dir "$CASES_DIR" --case "$CASE_ID" \
  --expected-revision "$CASE_REVISION" --input proposal.json

node service-renewals-cli.mjs propose \
  --cases-dir "$CASES_DIR" --case "$CASE_ID" \
  --expected-revision "$CASE_REVISION" --request-id "$REQUEST_ID" \
  --input proposal.json
~~~

To bind a reviewed preview, add its `previewSha256` as `expectedPreviewSha256` in the proposal input. Publishing a quote changes the case revision; reopen the case before attaching it. For that attachment, use the same renewal ID, its current integer edition, the current proposed terms edition and hash, and the selected `quoteId` plus `quoteSha256`. Omit `continuation` so the attachment selects the already reviewed proposed edition.

A decision input contains the renewal ID and current integer edition, `state`, `actor`, `observedAt`, and a note or reference. Acceptance also selects the original `acceptanceId`. Run it with `decide` using the current case revision and a fresh request ID.

~~~sh
node service-renewals-cli.mjs decide \
  --cases-dir "$CASES_DIR" --case "$CASE_ID" \
  --expected-revision "$CASE_REVISION" --request-id "$REQUEST_ID" \
  --input decision.json

node service-renewals-cli.mjs handover \
  --cases-dir "$CASES_DIR" --case "$CASE_ID" --renewal "$RENEWAL_ID" \
  > renewal-handover.json
~~~

`--input -` reads JSON from standard input. `read` and `handover` accept `--revision` to open a retained case revision. Timestamps use exact UTC form with milliseconds. Input files and standard input accept at most 128 KiB of JSON. Argument and operation errors emit a structured error on standard error and exit with status 1.

## Retry and concurrent edits

Keep the original request ID, case revision, and complete input unchanged for a retry. The wrapper retains the outer case revision as `input.expectedCaseRevision` in the core request. Its digest binds that revision and every supplied input to the original request ID. A repeated request returns the original renewal edition with `reused: true` and the current readable case view, without another save.

Reusing a request ID with changed inputs is a conflict. A new change must use a fresh request ID and current case/renewal/terms revisions. The case writer guards the save against concurrent edits; if another attempt has already saved the identical request, the wrapper reopens it and returns that retained result.

## Handover contents

`financialJoin` includes the original case and agreement IDs, selected case revision, exact source/proposed/active terms references, quote ID and hash, accepted-response ID, and original acceptance time. `quoteDocument` and `acceptance` are the original decoded commercial documents. Each material entry carries its original ID, SHA-256, byte length, and base64-encoded bytes. The exporter verifies those bytes against their retained hash and size.

The complete original case terms and renewal histories are included as `termsHistory` and `renewalHistory`. `acceptedHead` selects the exact accepted renewal edition from that history, including after the current renewal has been closed; it is null before acceptance.

The handover's `sha256` is the service canonical hash of the complete object before adding that final field. A selected historical case revision produces the renewal and documents available at that revision. The export includes the current agreement head at that selected revision alongside the exact edition activated by this renewal.

## Financial ingestion

Validate the complete handover before consuming it outside the case console. The exported helper checks the original terms and renewal histories, the selected accepted edition, every joined reference, the exact quote and response bytes, and the outer content hash. It returns the validated envelope with its original fields and seal.

~~~javascript
import {readFile} from 'node:fs/promises';
import {validateServiceRenewalHandover} from './service-renewals.mjs';

const handover = await validateServiceRenewalHandover(
  JSON.parse(await readFile('renewal-handover.json', 'utf8'))
);
if (!handover.acceptedHead) throw new Error('Choose an accepted renewal for financial ingestion.');
const quoteContent = Buffer.from(handover.materials.quote.data, 'base64').toString('utf8');
const responseContent = Buffer.from(handover.materials.acceptance.data, 'base64').toString('utf8');
const renewalJson = JSON.stringify(handover);
~~~

Pass `quoteContent` and `responseContent` as the original UTF-8 document strings. Preserve those bytes when retaining them; the material hashes identify the original encoding. Keep `renewalJson` alongside the financial record so its service continuation and acceptance remain available to downstream consumers.

`financialJoin.agreementId` is the original service terms UUID, equal to `sourceTerms.id`. A financial agreement can have its own UUID; retain that relationship explicitly. `acceptedHead` identifies the accepted renewal edition by `{id, revision, sha256}`, while `renewal` is the selected renewal's current full snapshot and can record a later closure.
